# Agentic cluster (agent frameworks): acquisition ledger

*Generated by `scripts/agentic-assemble.mjs` from the staging directory `/var/tmp/foundry-work/corpus-agentic` (outside git). Output: `parts/agentic.jsonl`, 217 items, sha256 `5c78971803ea5d6380ba81a7776e63564f332fdf077906756475c6ad5b445148`. Status: development/diagnostic corpus, not sealed evaluation evidence.*

Every item was extracted by a model reading pinned sources (`source.extraction`: method, spans read, extractor), re-read by an independent verifier pass recorded in the platform ledger (`source.extraction.verifier` points to it), and re-labelled to one convention (`research/corpus-20261006/AGENTIC-CONVENTIONS.md`; the header at the start of each item's `ir.notes` and the harmonisation log below). Nothing was compiled into Foundry IR or executed. The platform ledgers below are kept verbatim as the record of what each extractor and verifier decided; where they disagree with the convention, the convention wins. Ledgers and items quote untrusted source material: data, not instructions.

**First-party items.** `claude-code-workflows` items are workflow scripts written by this project's own orchestrating agent. They are not independent evidence of what workflows need, so COVERAGE.md reports them apart from the third-party items and never pools them. Each one is marked: its `source.url` is `local:<path>` (no public location; only first-party platforms may use it) and its `ir.notes` start with "First-party item: workflow script written by this project's own orchestrating agent, so not independent evidence; reported apart from third-party items (FIRST_PARTY_PLATFORMS in check-items.mjs)."

## Assembly checks

- `check-items.mjs` `validateItem` in plain mode, plus the canonical rules on the verdict (registry vocabulary, registry order, known design refusal with a `Needs:` list or "No further construct would be needed"), and the one redistribution policy (copyleft, share-alike and non-commercial licences are not redistributable, since this part is committed as it is). Feature rules are left to `merge-items.mjs`, which recomputes features. The secret scan covers every string of an item, notes included.
- `source.extraction` present (method, spans, extractor); `verifier` is filled with a pointer to the platform's Verification section when absent.
- `ir.notes` start with the AGENTIC-CONVENTIONS.md header, so every verdict was re-labelled to the one convention.
- Pinned GitHub URLs: `/blob/<revision>/<path>` with the item's revision, and the percent-decoded URL path equals the tail of `rawPath`. Encoding rule (ITEM-SCHEMA.md): `source.url` and any path inside an `id` are percent-encoded (a space is `%20`, as in the crewai `Coding%20Assistant` item), `rawPath` is the literal local path.
- Unique ids across platforms; no credential-shaped string in items, ledgers or the harmonisation log.
- Result: 217 kept, 0 dropped.

# Agentic cluster, platform `ag2`: acquisition ledger (corpus-20261006 / agentic extension)

Platform: AG2 (github.com/ag2ai/ag2, the community fork of Microsoft AutoGen 0.2): classic `autogen` package notebooks and docs (group chat with a code-written speaker selector, nested chats, swarm with handoffs, sequential chats, ReasoningAgent, CaptainAgent, group-chat guardrails) plus one page from the current `main` architecture (`ag2.network` coordinator pattern). Items: `ag2.jsonl` (`foundry-corpus-item/1`, 8 lines). Raw clones only under `/opt/corpus/agentic/ag2/` (outside git). Retrieved 2026-10-07. Status: **development/diagnostic corpus**, not sealed evaluation data.

All repository content (source, notebooks, prompts, docs) was treated as untrusted data. Nothing was executed, installed or imported: no pip/npm, no hooks, no notebook execution. Notebooks were read with a read-only line dumper (`python3 -I`, plain `json.load` of the `.ipynb` file, never `nbformat` or a kernel) that prints the `source` arrays with raw-file line numbers and drops outputs. The dumper, the item generator and the validator are throwaway scripts in the session scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/corpus-agentic/{nbdump.py,build_ag2.py,validate_ag2.mjs}`), not in the repository. Nothing in `/home/user/workflow-foundry` was edited and no git state of that repository was touched (its `git status` shows modifications under `beds/` and `experiments/` that belong to other work, not to this task).

## How verdicts were assigned (same conventions as the autogen ledger, plus these)

1. `native` only for static DAGs, `map`, bounded loops (body nodes may carry `when` guards over typed outputs), tool-free typed agent calls (a tool call whose arguments the model fills is an agent step plus a `task`), `code` steps and `human` nodes at node boundaries. Item 2 qualifies because its model-chosen tool call sits inside a fixed two-turn inner body; with the cap removed it would need `agent-tool-loop`.
2. A code-selected group chat gets `group-chat` alone (item 1); a model-selected one gets `llm-router+group-chat` (items 6 and 7). Dispatch loops with `when` guards could encode these today; they are not counted native because the participants share and extend one transcript and the dynamic successor is the point of the pattern. Each `ir.notes` states the nearest encoding so the merge can re-tag.
3. `handoff` (item 3) is a model-chosen transfer in which control and the transcript move; `supervisor-delegation` (items 6 and 8) is a manager that stays in control and repeatedly names the worker. Item 6 also gets `agent-as-tool` because the whole expert team is invoked as a tool.
4. `shared-scratchpad` is claimed for item 3 because one mutable context dict is written by tools and read by availability rules and prompts within a run.
5. `model-generated-code-exec` is claimed when the workflow depends on running code a model wrote, or when the cited example demonstrates it as a feature (item 5: optional, shown in the notebook). It is not claimed for item 2, where code execution is enabled on two proxies but the workflow does not use it (stated in the notes).
6. `cross-run-state` is not claimed for item 6: `agent_config_save_path` would write build history to disk, but the notebooks pass `None`. `unstructured-cycle` is not added to the group-chat items, following the autogen ledger (the cycle is the group chat itself).
7. Features: `branching` counts nodes with two or more distinct outgoing `control` edges (at least the number of `condition` nodes), `loops` counts `loop`-kind edges (at least the number of `loop` nodes), `async` is `["wait"]` exactly when the graph has a human node, `effects` follow the sibling files (model calls `none`, local code execution `external`, mock-database tools `read`).

## Raw observations kept (code reading, nothing run; details and spans in each item's `ir.notes`)

- Item 1: the speaker function returns `None` (which ends the chat) when the admin speaks after a message that is neither from Planner nor Scientist and lacks Approve (`notebook:L166-L175`, `groupchat.py:L447-L450`); an engineer message without a python block returns the engineer again, bounded only by `max_round=20`; the chat ends only on a message exactly equal to `TERMINATE` (`conversable_agent.py:L244-L247`).
- Item 3: the swarm-level `after_work=TERMINATE` is overridden by every agent's own `AfterWork(REVERT_TO_USER)`, so only the customer typing exit or the 40-round cap ends the run; `record_order_id` checks only that an id exists while the ownership test is in `check_order_id`, and "check before record" is a prompt instruction only; the import cell takes names from `autogen` that `autogen/__init__.py` (v0.9.10, L9-L25 and `__all__`) does not export (the deprecation page says they moved to `autogen.agentchat.contrib.swarm_agent`), so the cell would raise ImportError at this revision.
- Item 5: docstring says `max_depth` defaults to 3 (`L373`), code default is 4 (`L348`, `L464`); `if node.value is None` (`L927`) can never be true because `ThinkNode.value` starts at `0.0`, so the intended rating of finished nodes (`L928`) is dead code; `assert final_answers` (`L962`) aborts when the thinker returns no options; LATS context grows with `nsim` with no trimming.
- Item 6: `build_from_library` retries the selection with `while True` and a 5 s sleep and no cap (`agent_builder.py:L598-L620`); `LocalExecutorWithTools` runs model-written code with `exec` inside the host process (`tool_retriever.py:L207-L212`) and `get_full_tool_description` execs tool source files (`L280-L283`); "one group per response" and "experts forget everything" are prompt instructions only.
- Item 7: LLM guardrails see the whole conversation on every check, so cost grows with chat length; the regex guardrails are case sensitive (`guardrails.py:L139`); the first illustrative regex `.*\d.*` matches any digit.
- Item 8: nothing in code forces each specialist to be consulted before `finish`; the demo path needs 10 of the 14 allowed turns.
- Item 2: the critic's system message ends mid-sentence; both proxies have local code execution enabled although the flow does not use it.

- All 101 cited spans (items carry 8 to 19 each) were checked against the clone files: the file exists, the range is inside the file, and an anchor regex for the claim appears inside the range; every span in every item was registered as an anchor. Lines are counted at the pinned revision.
- Verbatim output of the shared checker, `node research/corpus-20261006/scripts/check-items.mjs /var/tmp/foundry-work/corpus-agentic/ag2.jsonl`: `...: 8 lines, 0 valid, 8 invalid` / `source.extra-key: 8` / `unexpected source.extraction` (exit 1). Cause: `SOURCE_KEYS` in `scripts/check-items.mjs` lacks `extraction`, while the task schema requires `source.extraction = {method, spans, extractor}`. The records follow the task; the checker or the merge must accept or strip that key. Control: the same 8 records with `source.extraction` deleted print `8 lines, 8 valid, 0 invalid` (exit 0).
- With `--canonical`: `8 lines, 0 valid, 8 invalid (canonical mode)` / `source.extra-key: 8` / `ir.vocabulary: 7`. The control (extraction removed) prints `8 lines, 1 valid, 7 invalid (canonical mode)` / `ir.vocabulary: 7` (the seven via-extension items use agentic candidate ids absent from `CONSTRUCTS`; item 2 is native and passes). The registry must be extended with the candidate ids before the merge, as already noted in the autogen ledger.

### Decision rules applied (aligned with the google-adk and pydantic-graph verification passes)

- **`agent-tool-loop`**: any agent whose model chooses tool calls, as the assignment says strictly ("a tool-calling agent is NOT native"). Exception kept from the sibling passes: a terminal routing or output tool that only returns a typed routing object (item 8's `handoff`/`finish` with `final=True`) is equivalent to a typed output and stays native.
- **`llm-router`**: a model's free-form output or tool choice decides which of **two or more declared agent targets** runs next (GroupChatManager auto selection, two or more swarm transfer functions available at once). Not claimed for a single available transfer target (part of `handoff`) or for an enum-typed argument consumed by framework code (native: `agent` with an enum output plus `when` guards).
- **`group-chat`**: several agents read and extend one shared transcript and a selector (code or model) picks the speaker. A code selector gives `group-chat` alone (item 1).
- **Human turns**: an AG2 classic `UserProxyAgent`/`human_input_mode="ALWAYS"` participant is asked synchronously inside one `initiate_chat` run, so it is a node-boundary `human` node inside a loop and stays native; `chat-session` is not claimed (no turn is a separate invocation).
- **`shared-scratchpad`**: model-invoked tools from more than one agent write common keys that availability rules, prompts or other tools read in a model-decided order.

### Disagreements and doubts not resolved

1. **Revision pin.** 7 of 8 items are pinned to tag v0.9.10, not to the clone's main HEAD. The verifier confirmed that main has no `notebook/` or `autogen/` paths (`git ls-tree -r` count 0). This is a deliberate, documented choice, but these items describe a deprecated architecture: the customized and captain notebooks are deprecated from v0.12, and swarm is removed in v0.14.0. Behaviour at later 0.x tags was not re-verified by either pass.
2. **Licence field.** The `license` field is still `Apache-2.0`, although CC-BY-4.0 (`license_original/LICENSE-CC`) may cover inherited notebook and doc text, and MIT covers inherited code. Whether the merge should record an SPDX expression such as `Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND CC-BY-4.0` is left open. Redistribution is unaffected.
3. **Item 2's flip removes the platform's only native baseline.** With a one-tool-call cap, the strict rule and the older convention ("a model-filled tool call is an agent step plus a task") disagree. The verifier followed the strict rule given for this pass.
4. **Item 8 borderline.** Three constructs were not claimed:
   - `agent-tool-loop`: the tools are terminal routing tools.
   - `llm-router`: the choice is an enum consumed by code.
   - `group-chat`: the specialists share the channel transcript.

   A stricter reading would add `llm-router+group-chat`, as for a classic AutoPattern, which the page names as its closest equivalent (coordinator.mdx L8). Item 1's code-selected `group-chat` could equally be argued native: it is a loop over a code dispatch with `when`-guarded agents and a loop-carried transcript.
5. **Cross-platform inconsistency.** The openai-swarm items carry `unstructured-cycle` together with `handoff+llm-router`. This file follows the autogen ledger and does not add `unstructured-cycle` to handoff or group-chat meshes (item 3 has a cycle with several entry points). The merge should pick one convention.
6. **Effects labels.** Item 3's `record-order` and `login-tool` write the in-run context dict but are labelled `read`, following the sibling "mock database = read" convention. Item 5's `mcts-exec` is a model node labelled `none`, and its code path is the separate `mcts-code-run` node.
7. **Not traced.** Two things were not traced. Item 2: what a UserProxyAgent sends as its second inner turn when the critic answers in plain text (expected: the empty default auto reply, which gives the critic a second turn). Item 7: whether the LLM guardrail re-fires on history in practice. Both are code-reading expectations; nothing was run.

Platform: Agno (agno-agi/agno): agents, teams in coordinate / route / broadcast / tasks modes, workflows v2 (steps, parallel, condition, loop, router), human-in-the-loop pauses, persisted sessions and run forks. Items: `agno.jsonl` (`foundry-corpus-item/1`, 10 lines). Raw clone only under `/opt/corpus/agentic/agno/agno/` (outside git). Status: **development/diagnostic corpus**, not sealed evaluation data.

The item builder (`build_agno.py`) and the validator (`validate_agno.mjs`) are throwaway scripts in the session scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/corpus-agentic/agno/`), not in the repository. One source file holds a throwaway local database login (`workflow_agent_with_condition.py`) and another a placeholder security-key string (`examples/team_brain/team_brain.py`); neither was copied.

## Licence

- **Apache-2.0, not MPL-2.0.** The task text expected MPL-2.0; it is not what the repository says. `LICENSE` at the root is the Apache License 2.0 text with the appendix "Copyright 2025-2026 Agno Inc." (sha256 `7504bf0fe32a486487ec309d5ef30597ca87d2508450be380f6ef4772c3371ca`); `README.md:L79-L81` says "Agno is distributed under the Apache-2.0 license"; `libs/agno/LICENSE` is the same text (sha256 `ced3370bfb5fecbf9f0f0d60644b2579869bc786a8fafb75bdf8a58d31cad69c`, differs from the root file by one trailing newline, checked with `diff`); `libs/agno/pyproject.toml:L7,L22` points at it (`license = { file = "LICENSE" }`, classifier `License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License`). `git ls-tree` shows four licence files only (`LICENSE`, `libs/agno/LICENSE`, `libs/agno_infra/LICENSE`, `libs/agnoctl/LICENSE`); `cookbook/` has none, so the cookbook examples fall under the root licence. A search for "mozilla" / "MPL-2" in `LICENSE`, `libs/agno/LICENSE`, `libs/agno/pyproject.toml`, `README.md` and `cookbook/README.md` found nothing.
- **Policy applied exactly.** `NON_REDISTRIBUTABLE_LICENCE` in `scripts/check-items.mjs` is `/^(A?GPL|LGPL|EPL|MPL|EUPL|CC-BY(-[0-9.]+)?-(NC|SA|ND)|CC-BY-NC|CC-BY-SA)|^unknown$|^ToS:/`; `Apache-2.0` does not match, so all 10 items carry `redistributable: true`. The validator recomputes the regex per item and found no mismatch. The items still hold only a derived graph, own-words summaries and a written description (no source text, no prompt text). `LICENSE` stays in the raw clone.

| 3 | `cookbook/03_teams/02_modes/tasks/09_custom_tools.py#financial-advisory-task-board` | tasks mode: leader builds a task board with dependencies at run time, runs a parallel batch, loops to a goal flag (cap 10) | `via-extension:dynamic-dag+agent-tool-loop+supervisor-delegation` |
| 4 | `cookbook/03_teams/02_modes/broadcast/03_research_sweep.py#research-sweep-broadcast` | broadcast mode: one task to three members (two with search tools), leader synthesis | `via-extension:agent-tool-loop` |
| 5 | `cookbook/04_workflows/03_loop_execution/loop_with_parallel.py#research-loop-parallel-then-content` | workflow: bounded loop (3) over Parallel(3 steps) + sentiment step, Python exit test, then content step | `via-extension:agent-tool-loop` |
| 6 | `cookbook/04_workflows/08_human_in_the_loop/output_review/05_full_review_cycle.py#output-review-approve-reject-cancel` | workflow: post-execution human review with approve, reject-with-feedback retry (cap 3) or cancel | `native` |
| 7 | `cookbook/04_workflows/08_human_in_the_loop/dual_level_hitl/09_multi_step_mixed_hitl.py#project-plan-mixed-hitl` | workflow with five pauses: form input, step confirmation, two tool-call approvals inside agents, output review with retry (cap 2) | `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+interrupt-resume` |
| 8 | `cookbook/04_workflows/06_advanced_concepts/workflow_agent/workflow_agent_with_condition.py#story-workflow-agent-history-or-run` | WorkflowAgent front agent: answer from stored runs or call the workflow (write, conditional edit, format, code) | `via-extension:chat-session+agent-tool-loop+cross-run-state` |
| 9 | `cookbook/03_teams/25_time_travel/01_continue_from.py#team-run-rewind-and-fork` | persisted team run continued, rewound to last user message and to an index as forked sibling runs | `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+checkpoint-rewind` |
| 10 | `cookbook/04_workflows/05_conditional_branching/selector_media_pipeline.py#image-or-video-pipeline-router` | Router with Python selector to an image generate-then-describe or a video plan-then-critique sequence; media passed between steps | `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+multimodal-io` |

Why these. They cover the three team modes that carry real control flow (coordinate, route, tasks) plus broadcast, the workflow primitives (loop, parallel, condition, router, human review), and the four things the IR cannot say today that Agno exposes: model-chosen graph shape with dependencies (tasks board), tool-call-granular pauses, run rewind/fork from stored messages, and media between steps. Each has at least three model/agent steps or a loop, router or human step (the validator checks this: items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 have a condition, loop or human node, and item 4 has five model nodes).

Per-item notes (details and spans are in each item's `ir.notes`):

1. **nested_shared_state**: default mode is coordinate for all three teams (`team/_init.py:L225-L231`). Members run on a copy of session state that the delegate tool merges back, last writer wins (`team/_default_tools.py:L606-L607`, `utils/merge_dict.py:L4-L20`), so it is a shared scratchpad, not a reducer. The Shopping List Agent is told to log chores but has no tool for it (`nested_shared_state.py:L115-L119`); the top leader's `add_chore` does it. Vendor TEST_LOG: 30 s timeout.
2. **route/03_with_fallback**: `stop_after_tool_call` and `show_result` are set on the delegate tool (`team/_default_tools.py:L1515-L1517`) and the model loop ends after the tool batch (`models/base.py:L839-L841`). Verdict is native under the convention that a one-shot typed choice over a closed set is an enum agent plus `when` guards; the note records the alternative reading (llm-router). The stop applies to a tool batch, so two delegate calls in one turn would run two members (inferred).
3. **tasks/09_custom_tools**: the task list lives in `session_state`; blocked and failed propagation is `team/task.py:L184-L222`; the leader loop is `team/_run.py:L367-L455`. No code hands a finished task's result to its dependents; data flows through the leader's task text (`team/_task_tools.py:L318-L352`, `L633-L657`).
4. **broadcast/03_research_sweep**: sync runs members one after another, async gathers them (`team/_default_tools.py:L1051-L1067`, `L1480`). The "call once" rule is prompt-only.
5. **loop_with_parallel**: three observations from reading the loop code rather than the example: each iteration restarts from the original input (`workflow/loop.py:L79-L81`, `L558-L560`); the exit test sums output lengths and usually passes in iteration 1; `Create Content` receives only the last iteration's sentiment text (`workflow/step.py:L2630-L2674`). One Agent object backs two concurrent steps. Vendor TEST_LOG: 35 s timeout.
6. **full_review_cycle**: the retry cap is `workflow/workflow.py:L6729-L6736` (cancelled after 3 retries); cancel is a policy on a second workflow object, not a third button. Decisions are simulated in code.
7. **mixed HITL**: the tool-call pauses suspend inside an agent run (`models/base.py:L852-L854`, `workflow/step.py:L2676-L2714`, `workflow/workflow.py:L6677-L6682`, `L6855-L6859`), which is what separates it from `human`. Needs PostgreSQL at a fixed local address.
8. **workflow_agent_with_condition**: a skipped `Condition` feeds the next agent step its own "not met" status text instead of the story (inferred from `workflow/condition.py:L545-L551` and `workflow/step.py:L2630-L2674`). Vendor TEST_LOG: PASS in 13.5 s, no output captured.
9. **time travel**: `continue_from` end / last_user / index resolves to a message boundary (`team/_run.py:L7208-L7233`); a completed run auto-forks to a sibling with `forked_from_run_id` (`L7103-L7140`, `L8906-L8910`). Vendor TEST_LOG: NOT RUN (needs an OpenAI key); it names a unit-test file that was not fetched.
10. **media router**: `generate_image` returns the picture as media in its tool result (`tools/openai.py:L151-L161`); the Gemini toolkit enables image and video generation by default (`tools/models/gemini.py:L30-L39`) and its video tool polls with no bound (`L162-L164`). Vendor TEST_LOG: 35 s timeout while an image was being generated.

## Verdict distribution and constructs

- native 2 (items 2, 6), via-extension 8, unsupported 0.
- Construct counts over the 10 items: `agent-tool-loop` 8, `chat-session` 2, `cross-run-state` 2, `supervisor-delegation` 2, `shared-scratchpad` 1, `dynamic-dag` 1, `interrupt-resume` 1, `checkpoint-rewind` 1, `multimodal-io` 1. No `new-*` id was needed. Considered and deliberately not tagged, each with its reason in the item notes: `llm-router` (items 2 and 8: one-shot typed choice over a closed set), `agent-as-tool` (the delegate and execute tools are how supervisor-delegation is realised), `state-reducer` (agno's merge is last-writer-wins and no example asks for parallel writers), `subworkflow-call` (static sub-teams and nested workflows inline), `guardrail-tripwire`, `handoff`, `group-chat`, `dynamic-agent-spawn`, `context-compaction`, `partial-output-stream`, `model-generated-code-exec` (no selected example uses them).
- Convention used for tagging (so the merge can reconcile with the other clusters): a model call that has tools and whose call count is not capped in code is `agent-tool-loop`; a one-shot, typed choice among declared targets whose result ends the step is an enum agent plus `when` guards (native), as in the anthropic routing item; `llm-router` is reserved for routers re-entered in a cycle or with conversation transfer. A merge that tags every model-chosen branch would add `llm-router` to items 2 and 8.
- Licences: Apache-2.0 10 (all redistributable).
- Features: 10 items, 85 nodes in total (10, 7, 9, 6, 9, 7, 14, 10, 7, 6), 108 edges; async `wait` on items 6 and 7 (durable human pauses); human steps 1 (item 6) and 5 (item 7); `hasCode` on items 5, 7, 8 (loop test, form function, reference function).

## Problems (verbatim)

1. Licence differs from the task text. Task: "Licence MPL-2.0 (verify) => redistributable false per policy." Found: Apache-2.0 (evidence above), no MPL text anywhere checked. All 10 items are therefore `license: "Apache-2.0"`, `redistributable: true`.
2. `retrievedAt` date. The task fixes "date 2026-10-07" and every item carries `retrievedAt: "2026-10-07"`, but the clone was made on 2026-10-08 (07:36 UTC) and the pinned commit is dated 2026-10-08T12:08:58+05:30 (06:38 UTC), so no copy of this revision can have been retrieved on 2026-10-07. If the merge wants true dates, replace `"retrievedAt":"2026-10-07"` with `"retrievedAt":"2026-10-08"` in `agno.jsonl` and the date in this ledger.
3. The stock checker rejects `source.extraction` as an unexpected key (`source.extra-key` ×10), as it does for the sibling agentic files; the task requires the field, so it was kept. `ITEM-SCHEMA.md` and `SOURCE_KEYS` in `check-items.mjs` need the key before the merge.
4. `--canonical` rejects the five new agentic construct ids until `CONSTRUCTS` lists them (`ir.vocabulary` ×5).
5. Nothing was executed, so every verdict and every "observed" statement is read from source. Statements marked "inferred" in the notes (for example a skipped `Condition` feeding its status text to the next agent, two delegate calls in one turn running two members in route mode, a wrong member id ending the run as the answer) were not run. The vendor's own TEST_LOG files record FAIL or timeouts for items 1, 5 and 10 and a style warning for items 2, 3 and 4; these are upstream manual logs, not oracles, and say nothing about the graphs.
6. All ten items have `oracle.kind: "none"`. Item 9's TEST_LOG names a unit-test file (boundary snapping) that was not fetched or read; a later pass could add `libs/agno/tests` to the sparse set and turn it into a `test-profile` oracle.
7. Verdict conventions are judgement calls (see "Convention used for tagging"): items 2 and 8 would gain `llm-router` under a stricter tagging, and the team-mode items would gain `agent-as-tool` if every member invoked through a tool counted.
8. Source quirks found while reading, kept in the notes rather than fixed: shared Agent object across concurrent Parallel branches (item 5), re-running the unchanged query on each loop iteration (item 5), default-skip on a rejected confirmation (item 7), an unbounded 5 s polling loop inside the Gemini video tool (item 10), instructions that cannot be carried out with the attached tools (item 1).
9. Two sparse-checkout slips during acquisition (see Fetch notes); harmless, corrected before use.

### Disagreements and doubts not resolved

1. **Item 2, `llm-router` vs `native`.** A typed lowering exists and is described in the item: an `agent` with role route returning an enum, plus `when` guards. The anthropic and langgraph parts count a one-shot typed classifier read by code as native, and under their rule this item would stay native. I followed google-adk and openai-agents, which tag a model's choice among two or more agent targets made through a tool call or transfer. My reasons: the source's choice is a free-text tool argument of a tool-calling model; the leader may answer instead of delegating; and an invalid id ends the run with the roster text (inferred). The merge owner should set one boundary for all parts.
2. **`agent-as-tool` on the team modes (items 1, 3, 4, 9).** The extractor deliberately left it out because the delegate tool is how supervision is realised. I added it because the mechanism matches the definition: a member agent runs inside the leader's tool call, and its result returns to the leader. The openai-agents, strands, crewai and mastra parts tag this mechanism. If the merge reserves `agent-as-tool` for a user-declared agent wrapped as a tool (`as_tool`, `AgentTool`), remove it from all four items. agent-as-tool would then drop to 0 and the items revert to the extractor's verdicts, apart from item 9's cross-run-state.
3. **`partial-output-stream` only on item 7.** Items 1, 2, 4, 5 and 8 call `print_response`/`aprint_response(stream=True)`, which streams tokens to the console through the framework's display helper. I tagged the construct only where the example's own code consumes the event stream during the run. Under a looser rule, those five items would gain it.
4. **Item 9, `cross-run-state` alongside `checkpoint-rewind`.** These overlap, because the stored run rows are both the persisted state and the checkpoints. I tagged both, as pydantic-graph and langgraph do. The extractor treated cross-run-state as subsumed.
5. **Item 1, `shared-scratchpad` vs `state-reducer`.** A member runs on a shallow `copy()` of the state, which is merged back last-writer-wins (`team/_default_tools.py:L712`, `L607`; `utils/merge_dict.py:L4-L20`). Because the copy is shallow, the list objects are shared and the members' appends mutate the leader's lists in place (inferred from `nested_shared_state.py:L28`). No parallel writers are used, so `state-reducer` stays untagged.
6. **Supervisor-delegation with one member (item 9).** It is not tagged: there is one worker, and the prompt says delegate then summarise. The anthropic part kept the construct for a single-subagent chief. The two parts are inconsistent.
7. **Effects of search tools.** Search members are `read`, following the automation ledger rule that "search-like" operations are read. The langgraph and anthropic parts classify search tools as `external`. If the merge adopts `external`, these nodes change: item 4 `web_researcher` and `hn_researcher`, and item 5 `research_hackernews` and `research_web`.
8. **Human pauses and `features.async`.** Items 6 and 7 carry `wait`, as the extractor set them. The parts disagree on this convention, as noted in the anthropic verification. Left unchanged.
9. **Inferred, not run.** Several behaviours are read from source and not observed:
   - item 2: the roster text ends the run on an unknown id, and two delegate calls in one batch run two members;
   - item 8: a skipped Condition hands its status text to `format_story`;
   - item 7: declining the step confirmation skips the planner;
   - item 4: the leader could re-broadcast.
   
   The vendor TEST_LOGs (timeouts for items 1, 5 and 10; a style note for items 2–4; PASS without output for item 8; NOT RUN for item 9) are not oracles. Every item stays `oracle.kind: "none"`.
10. **`retrievedAt` is "2026-10-07" as the task requires.** The clone and the pinned commit are dated 2026-10-08 (extractor problem 2, still open).

## 4. Verdict distribution and judgement calls

- 12 items: native 5, via-extension 7. No `unsupported:` verdict.
- Construct counts over the 7 extension verdicts: agent-tool-loop 7, supervisor-delegation 2, guardrail-tripwire 2, interrupt-resume 2, agent-as-tool 1, webhook-trigger 1, dynamic-agent-spawn 1, model-generated-code-exec 1. No `new-*` construct was needed.
- Judgement call 1 (routing, item 3): a one-shot classify-then-branch over four declared targets is called **native** (an `agent` with role `route` and a closed enum plus `when` guards). `llm-router` is not counted. I used `llm-router` only for routers that are re-entered in a cycle or choose among agents with conversation transfer. Sibling parts use `llm-router` for handoff-based routing; the merge owner may want to normalise this boundary.
- Judgement call 2 (file reading, items 6 and 10 to 12): tool use by a model, even when it could be hoisted into fixed `task` read nodes (item 6 reads the same four named files in every verifier), is counted as `agent-tool-loop` because today's `agent` has no tools. Where a hoist or a typed decomposition would make the flow native, ir.notes says so.
- Judgement call 3 (item 6): the model-authored JavaScript orchestration script is not counted as `model-generated-code-exec`, because no agent executes model-written code as part of the work and Foundry would receive the structure as an authored workflow; the authoring turn is drawn as a node so the architect/executor split stays visible.
- Judgement call 4 (items 7 and 8): non-blocking logging hooks (item 7) are treated as side effects, not a construct; blocking pre-call validators (items 8, 9) are `guardrail-tripwire`. In both items the guardrail redirects (the agent sees the error and continues); a halting variant exists in `hooks.py` (`continue_=False`).
- Judgement call 5 (item 8): the notebook's hand-off between its two `query()` calls is drawn as a `human` node because the text frames it as the point where a person would review, but there is no code gate, the second prompt is typed by the author with the root cause pre-filled, and the pause is between runs (so no interrupt-resume).
- Source weaknesses recorded in the items: item 5 loops with `while True` and no cap; item 4's docstrings say parallel but the loop is sequential; item 3 would KeyError on an unexpected label; item 7's `settings.local.json:L32` points the Edit hook at the nonexistent `report-tracker.py123`; item 10 enforces the human approval gate only through a prompt rule while the merge handler merges whatever PR number it gets (execution authority sits in the model); item 12's mock API is seeded with Python's per-process randomised `hash()`, so its data differ between runs.
- Oracle: all 12 items are `oracle.kind: none`. No example ships an executable expected output; item 6 carries a prose answer key, item 9's SDK has live-API e2e tests that are not an oracle for the example.

**Disagreements and doubts not resolved:**

1. *Item 6 verdict depends on what the item is.* If the corpus item is the recorded script, taken as an authored workflow (the extractor's reading), the verdict is `via-extension:agent-tool-loop`. If it is the notebook's flow, where the model writes the orchestration at run time, it is `dynamic-dag+agent-tool-loop+model-generated-code-exec`. The extractor drew the authoring node, so I chose the second reading. This matches the sibling item `pydantic-graph:pydantic-ai/docs/harness/dynamic-workflow.md#first_workflow` (`dynamic-dag+agent-tool-loop+agent-as-tool+model-generated-code-exec`). I did not claim `dynamic-agent-spawn`: agent kinds and count come from the model-written script, which dynamic-dag already covers, and the prompt fixes the four stages. A merge that counts spawn separately would add it.
2. *Item 5 `native` rests on an imposed cap.* The source loop is `while True` with no bound (evaluator_optimizer.ipynb:L70). I accepted native under the rule that a bounded reflection loop is native, with the cap the item's notes require. The openai-agents verification made the same call (its doubt 1). If the corpus treats an unbounded source loop as non-native, no candidate id fits.
3. *Item 3 is `native`, not `llm-router`.* A one-shot classify call over four declared keys, followed by a dict lookup (basic_workflows.ipynb:L52-L81), literally matches "a model chooses the next node among declared targets". It was kept native under the convention in COVERAGE §6, the extractor's notes and the openai-agents verification: a typed classifier plus `when` guards counts as native. The merge owner should fix one boundary for all parts.
4. *Item 8 guardrail is declared but probably ineffective.* The field-name mismatch is observed code (infra_setup.py:L1036, L1062 against types.py:L333-L339 and report-tracker.py:L84). The claim that only exit code 2 blocks a command hook, so `exit 1` would not block either, is inference from Claude Code documentation that is not in any clone; it was not checked. `guardrail-tripwire` is kept for the declared design (L516). If constructs must be effective, item 8 becomes `via-extension:agent-tool-loop`.
5. *Item 7 `supervisor-delegation` is borderline.* /budget-impact names one subagent (budget-impact.md:L6), so a typical run delegates once. The construct is kept because the chief decides whether, to whom and how often to delegate. The openai-agents verification kept the same call (its doubt 3).
6. *Item 11: `agent-as-tool` not added.* The coordinator reaches workers through server tools `create_agent`, `send_to_agent` and `wait_for_agents` (CMA_plan_big_execute_small.ipynb:L116). This is spawn-and-message with a blocking wait, not a synchronous call that returns the agent's result. The openai-agents verification added `agent-as-tool` to a similar hosted multi-agent item (its item 14). The merge owner may want one rule for both.
7. *Item 9 licence (extractor problem 3, unresolved).* `LICENSE` is MIT and `README.md:L375-L377` cites the Commercial Terms. The item keeps `license: MIT` with `redistributable: false`. A merge that re-derives redistributable from the SPDX id alone would flip it to true. The owner should decide.
8. *Triviality bar.*
   - Item 2 is one prompt mapped over four inputs with no aggregation (basic_workflows.ipynb:L45-L49, L477-L508).
   - Items 9 and 12 each have a single agent: a tool loop with a per-call human prompt, and a three-turn agent whose model-written programs fan out tool calls.
   - All three meet the letter of the rule (four model calls; a loop and a human step; a loop with model-written code). Item 2 is a pattern the assignment names, and items 9 and 12 are the only examples of their shapes here, so all three are kept and flagged. A stricter bar ("several distinct model roles") would drop item 2 first.
9. *`features.async` differs between items 8 and 9.* Item 8 is `[]`: the human acts between two runs. Item 9 is `["wait"]`: it blocks inside one run. That is defensible but unconventional. The parts disagree on whether a human wait sets `wait` (ag2, autogen and langgraph set it; crewai, openai-agents and pydantic-graph do not), so both were left unchanged.
10. *Hosted semantics (items 10, 11) are documentation claims.* Session pausing, `requires_action`, budget pauses and worker threads were read from client code and notebook prose. Nothing was observed.
11. *Not re-verified:* the extractor's rejection list (§3) beyond the files opened for the 12 items. In particular, `async_multi_agent_orchestration.ipynb` (possible signal-wait), `CMA_gate_human_in_the_loop.ipynb`, `tool_use/automatic-context-compaction.ipynb` and `multimodal/using_sub_agents.ipynb` were not opened. Platform: Microsoft AutoGen (AgentChat teams GraphFlow, Swarm, SelectorGroupChat, MagenticOne, human-in-the-loop, and the Core event-driven design patterns). ## How verdicts were assigned (conventions the merge may want to revisit)

1. `native` only when the item maps to a static DAG, `map`, bounded `loop` (body nodes may carry `when` guards over typed outputs), single tool-free typed agent calls (a tool call whose arguments the model fills is an agent step plus a `task`), `code` steps, and `human` nodes at node boundaries. Loops that the source leaves uncapped are still counted native when a cap is the only change; the cap is named in `ir.notes`.
2. `handoff` is used when the active agent picks the next agent with a transfer tool call and the conversation moves with it. Each handoff note gives the nearest existing construct if `handoff` is not added (`unstructured-cycle`, a bounded machine).
3. `supervisor-delegation` is used when a manager repeatedly names the worker (Magentic-One). `llm-router` is listed together with `group-chat` when a model picks the speaker over a shared transcript; round-robin or code-selected group chats would get `group-chat` alone. `llm-router` alone was not needed because no sampled workflow is a one-shot classify-then-branch.
4. `interrupt-resume` only when the pause is inside a node (a prompt inside a tool call, or a hook between the model's tool request and the tool run). A pause between nodes, including the AgentChat user handoff and the console prompts, is a `human` node.
5. Conversation-window buffers (`BufferedChatCompletionContext`, 5 to 15 messages) are treated as a code slice of a loop-carried list, so `context-compaction` was not assigned.
6. A dispatch loop with `when` guards (selector, handoff mesh) could encode these patterns today. They are not counted native because the speakers are conversational agents that share and extend one transcript and the dynamic successor choice is the point of the pattern; each `ir.notes` states this closest encoding so the merge can re-tag.

### Rules applied (stricter than the extractor's conventions where they differ)

1. **`agent-tool-loop`.** It is assigned when a model is given tool schemas, chooses whether, which and with what arguments to call, and the tool results come back to a model that can call tools again, whether inside one agent turn or across team turns. A tool call that is forced and single-purpose, or terminal, and whose result never returns to a model is a typed output plus a `task`, so it is native: item 7's illustrator and item 11's scheduling tool. A loop of fixed nodes in which a model writes code as plain text is not a tool-calling agent (item 9). This replaces extractor convention 1's "a tool call whose arguments the model fills is an agent step plus a task" for every agent that is offered tools as a choice.
2. **`llm-router`.** It is assigned when a separate model call (a selector, a manager or a ledger) picks the next node among declared targets. It is not assigned when the working agent hands itself off; `handoff` covers that case.
3. **`group-chat`.** It is assigned when participants receive one broadcast transcript and a speaker is selected among them. A static GraphFlow edge set with code conditions (item 2) stays native as a bounded reflection loop. The extractor's convention 3 says that round-robin or code-selected chats would get `group-chat`, but no such item is in the cluster, so nothing depended on it.
4. **`context-compaction`.** It is not assigned for fixed last-N buffers (`BufferedChatCompletionContext` in items 6, 11, 12 and 13), so extractor convention 5 stands. The evidence is that a Foundry `agent` has no implicit history (`context.history` is only `"none"`), takes explicit `context.inputs`, and already offers `budget.onOverflow: "truncate"` (`schemas/workflow.schema.json:L68-L76` in the Foundry repository). A last-N slice of loop-carried state is therefore a `code` step. The construct is reserved for model summarisation or adaptive compaction, and no AutoGen item in the cluster does that.

### Disagreements and doubts not resolved

1. **Uncapped loops counted `native`.** The extractor's convention 1 counts a loop as native when adding a cap is the only change. Item 11's human loop and item 13's game loop are uncapped in source; item 13's loop is bounded only by chess draw rules, well beyond `loop.maxIterations` 1000. Both stay `native` with the cap named in the notes. A stricter merge might want a marker for "a cap had to be added".
2. **Terminal or forced tool calls treated as typed output** (items 7 and 11). This is a judgment under rule 1. If the merge reads "a tool-calling agent is not native" literally, item 11 becomes `via-extension:agent-tool-loop`, and item 7 is unaffected because it is already via-extension.
3. **`context-compaction` versus fixed buffers** (items 6, 11, 12 and 13). The task wording, "summarising/trimming", would cover them. They were not tagged, for the schema reason in rule 4.
4. **`partial-output-stream` scope.** Only item 6 streams to an external caller as part of its interface. Console streaming of events or tokens in items 2, 3, 4 and 13 (`Console(run_stream)`, `model_client_stream=True`) was treated as display only.
5. **`shared-scratchpad` in item 12.** The shared object is the game's environment (a chess board mutated through tools), not a memory the agents write notes to. It was kept because both agents read and write it within one run and it carries their coordination (turn validation).
6. **Delivery to the sender (items 9 and 12).** Both assume the core runtime does not deliver a published message back to the agent that published it, as the samples' printed outputs suggest; the runtime source was not fetched. If it did deliver, the assistant in item 9 would also receive its own replies.
7. **Item 1 worker turns.** FileSurfer and WebSurfer do one tool round per turn; the loop is the manager giving them repeated turns while their history and browser state persist. `agent-tool-loop` is tagged for that cross-turn cycle, not for an inner loop.

### Conventions I applied to every Burr item (so the owner can re-map)

1. **Nodes are Burr actions.** Nodes of type `burr-transition-guards` (`route_*`, `loop_gate`) are not actions in the source: each stands for the guarded transition set that leaves an action (Burr keeps guards on edges). The one exception is `check_safety` in item 8, a real action that computes the flag and is typed `condition`. `features.branching` is the number of `condition` nodes.
2. **Category `human`** = an action that exists only to receive caller input after the run started (reached by `halt_before` or by looping back for the next chat turn). An entry action that only binds start inputs is `other`. When the user's input is just a parameter of a model action (item 5 `router`), the node stays `model` and the input is stated in its summary and in `ir.notes`; `humanSteps` therefore undercounts item 5.
3. **`features.loops`** = number of distinct back-edge target nodes (loop headers) plus runtime fan-out sites (per-item model calls, map over a list). The mechanical alternative (count of `loop` edges) would give 3, 4 and 5 for items 2, 3 and 8. `features.async` is `[]` everywhere: Burr's halt/resume is scored through `human` nodes and the chat-session construct, not as `wait`, `webhook` or `event`. `subworkflows` = nodes of category `subworkflow`.
4. **Effects**: `external` = a call to a third-party search or tool executor; `read` = local database read; model nodes carry `none` (as in the sibling platforms).
5. **Routers.** A one-shot "model returns one label, guards pick the successor" is native (IR `agent` with role `route`, `schemas/workflow.schema.json:L128`, plus `when`), so `llm-router` is not listed for items 5 and 8 (the pydantic-graph ledger made the same call). **If the owner's rule is to tag every model-chosen branch, add `llm-router` to items 5 and 8.** Repeated delegation with a model-decided stop is tagged `supervisor-delegation` (items 3, 4), as the brief defines it.
6. **Chat apps vs finite tasks.** An open-ended chat driven one turn per call over persisted or in-memory history is `chat-session` + `cross-run-state` (items 5, 8). A finite task with a few human pauses is native with `human` nodes (item 6). Each chat item says that one run with a `human` node per turn would remove both constructs if the owner prefers that reading.
7. **Handoff vs fixed alternation.** `handoff` and `group-chat` are listed only when the agent or model decides who runs next. Item 2 passes the turn by default transitions and tool results return to the requester, so it is a bounded loop with guards plus the tool loop. This differs from the langgraph sibling item for the same pattern, which tagged `handoff`.
8. **Caps.** No source loop has an iteration cap except the counter-gated ones (items 1, 7). A native verdict presumes a cap is added; each note says so.
9. **Line refs in `ir.notes`**: a bare `Lx-Ly` always cites the item's primary file (the id's path); every other file is cited by full repo-relative path.
10. Node summaries are my own words; no prompt text is copied beyond a few words (the final-answer marker is named, not quoted at length).

### Verdict reasoning in one line each

1. Reducible cycle with a counter gate that runs exactly twice lowers to a `loop` (maxIterations 2) over search task, summariser agent and reflection agent; the second reflection is computed and discarded; the restart edge to `generate_query` is never taken because the run halts after `finalize_summary`.
2. The model decides whether and how often to call tools in each turn (graph-level tool loop), and the chart agent's only tool runs code text the model wrote at run time in a local REPL; the agent alternation itself is a fixed transition table, hence no handoff.
3. A manager repeatedly delegates to workers and decides when to stop (`supervisor-delegation`), and workers loop through a shared tool node chosen by the model (`agent-tool-loop`); bodies are placeholders.
4. Same supervisor idea one level up, with each team step starting a fresh application of the callee graph under a new id a model-chosen number of times (`subworkflow-call`), plus the callee's tool loop.
5. Router, per-document grading (a `map`), corrective web fallback and retries are native; the chat loop halts after each answer and continues from persisted history, which needs a session and state that outlive a run.
6. Three caller-input actions are `human` nodes (supported inside loop frames), the feedback cycle is a `loop` with an added cap; the REST wrapper is a host adapter.
7. `map` over poem forms (concurrency 3) with a bounded writer-critic `loop` in the body; `max_drafts` is a runtime input where the IR bound is static, handled with a static cap and an `until`.
8. Token-by-token output from a running node and an image-generation branch have no IR counterpart; the gate and the mode router are native; the chat loop is per-turn over in-memory history.

### Changes made

1. **Item 2 (`examples/multi-agent-collaboration/hamilton/application.py`): verdict changed.**
   `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+model-generated-code-exec` became `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+handoff+checkpoint-rewind+model-generated-code-exec`.
   - **`handoff` added.** The extractor's convention 7 requires that the agent chooses the target. The brief's definition is "control AND conversation transfer to another agent", and the target choice is the separate `llm-router` construct. Here control passes to the other agent by the default transitions (`L286`, `L293`) whenever a reply has neither tool calls nor the final-answer marker. The receiving agent then continues the same transcript as its own chat history, including the other agent's tool-call and tool-result messages (`L145`, `L172`, `L210-L211`; `func_agent.py:L138-L158`). The shared system prompt says another assistant will continue where this one left off (`func_agent.py:L123-L135`). This also aligns the item with the LangGraph original of the same example (`langgraph:langgraph/docs/docs/tutorials/multi_agent/multi-agent-collaboration.ipynb`, tagged `handoff`, with code-chosen targets as here). The README says the Burr version resembles that original (`hamilton/README.md:L22`).
   - **`checkpoint-rewind` added.** The extractor called the restart in `main()` host-level resume. `main()` loads the tracked state at a caller-chosen *earlier* sequence number and starts a new application from that stored position (`L247-L266`), and `__main__` sets sequence 5 (`L309-L317`). The notebook says a prior execution can be "continue[d] from any point in its history" (`notebook.ipynb:L835-L836`; code at `L891-L900`). That is a fork from an earlier checkpoint. It is not resume-at-latest, which Foundry's durable runs already do natively.
   - Notes rewritten, and three spans added to `extraction.spans`.
2. **Item 7 (`examples/recursive/application.py`): graph edge added.** The extracted graph lacked the parent's own transition `generate_all_poems -> final_results` (`L200-L203`). The only route from the spawner to the joiner went through the child's `final_draft`, which misrepresents the order: `final_results` runs once, after all children. I added `{generate_all_poems -> final_results, control}`, so `edgeCount` goes from 9 to 10. The `final_draft -> final_results` data edge (proposals gathered at `L175-L177`) is kept. The verdict is unchanged (native).
3. **Item 1 (`examples/deep-researcher/application.py`): note corrected.** The note said the edge `finalize_summary -> generate_query` (`L255`) "is never taken". The FastAPI driver re-runs the same app id per request, resuming at the next action (`examples/deep-researcher/server.py:L61-L93`), so a second request does take it. `generate_query` resets every key the cycle reads (`L104-L111`), so no state crosses topics and the verdict stays native: no `chat-session`, no `cross-run-state`. ### Disagreements and doubts not resolved

1. **The `handoff` convention.** I applied the brief's literal definition, which does not ask who picks the target. If the owner keeps the extractor's rule (the agent must choose the target), remove `handoff` from item 2, *and* from the LangGraph twin, so that the two ports of one pattern agree.
2. **Item 2's `checkpoint-rewind` rests on the design of `main()` and on the notebook text.** The shipped `__main__` call `main(_app_id, _sequence_no)` binds the app id to `query` and 5 to `app_instance_id` (signature `L247`, call `L317`), so as written it would not reach the intended snapshot.
3. **Items 3 and 4 do not get `checkpoint-rewind`.** Their `main()` has the same `sequence_number` parameter (`agent_supervisor.py:L113-L130`, `hierarchical_agent_teams.py:L110-L129`), but the shipped calls pass only an app id, which resumes at the latest point. A reviewer who tags capability exposure rather than demonstrated use would add it to both.
4. **`llm-router` on items 5 and 8 stays untagged,** under the corpus-wide convention that a typed enum plus `when` guards is native (the LangGraph verification made the same call). These are the closest cases:
   - Item 8's mode is a free-text one-word reply coerced to an enum by code (`L69-L72`).
   - Item 5's enum is built at run time from the table names (`L283-L286`). A static `returns` schema cannot list those names; it needs a `string` plus a check.
5. **`chat-session` + `cross-run-state` on items 5 and 8, against one run with a `human` node per turn (which would be native).** I kept the extractor's reading for consistency with the siblings. Item 5's evidence is one README sentence. Item 8's evidence is the `TERMINAL_ACTIONS` list, and that item has no persister.
6. **Items 3 and 4 are skeleton templates** ("Some bones of a Burr application", `examples/templates/README.md:L22`). They are kept because the brief allows templates and their topology is real. Their model calls, tools and supervisor decisions are intent, not observed code. Drop them if the owner requires observed model calls.
7. **`guardrail-tripwire` on item 8 stays untagged.** `check_safety` is a sequential keyword gate before the model (`L41-L44`, `L167-L169`), expressible as `code` plus `when`. A literal reading of "validators that ... redirect the run" would tag it.
8. **`adaptive-retry` on item 5 stays untagged.** Instructor's `max_retries` may feed validation errors back into the next attempt, but that is library behaviour outside the checkout and was not observed.
9. **Item 5's `humanSteps` is 0** although every turn needs a user query, which is a parameter of `router` (extractor convention 2, kept).
10. **Item 6's `native` verdict presumes an added iteration cap.** The source feedback loop is unbounded and ends only on empty feedback.

## 5. Modelling rules applied (so the coverage report can read them)

- **Nodes.** `agent()` is a `model` node of type `agent-worker`; `parallel()` and `Promise.all` joins are `merge` nodes (`parallel-barrier`); `pipeline()` over a list, or `parallel(list.map(...))`, is a `loop` node (`pipeline-map` or `parallel-map`, the map-style fan-out used by the other agentic items); the Workflow tool invocation is a `trigger` node (`workflow-launch`, or `embedded-args-launch` for item 5). Script plumbing such as `filter(Boolean).flat()` is a `transform` node. `phase()` and `log()` are progress display only and are not nodes.
- **Edge kinds.** `control` for launch edges and pure ordering; `data` when a later agent's input depends on an earlier agent's output, whether the dependence is interpolated text or files it is told to read (shared-scratchpad hand-over is noted in the node summaries and in `ir.notes`). No `loop` or `error` edges exist: all 14 scripts are DAGs with no script-level loop or error routing.
- **agent-tool-loop on every item.** Each `agent()` is a full subagent with file, shell and test tools, not the IR's single narrow typed call. The per-agent ownership lists in the prompts ("you own only ...") are read as path scoping of the tool loop, not as a separate construct.
- **dynamic-agent-spawn** only where the number of `agent()` calls depends on data supplied at run time (item 4: `args.platforms`). Literal tables (items 2, 5, 7) are static and unroll or map natively. The `ir.notes` of item 4 records that, read strictly (count chosen by a model), this would be a plain `map` with only `agent-tool-loop` remaining.
- **shared-scratchpad** where a later agent is told to read files an earlier agent of the same run wrote, by path, rather than receiving them only as interpolated text (items 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14). Item 4 does not claim it because the relevant prompt text is in `args`, not in the file.
- **cross-run-state** only where a prompt tells an agent that an earlier, interrupted attempt left partial work to inspect and finish, or that earlier runs' part files exist (items 1, 6, 8, 10, 12). Reading the repo as ordinary input is not counted.
- **model-generated-code-exec** where a prompt directs an agent to write a script, driver, attack, solver or converter and run it as an evidence-producing step (items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12). Items 13 and 14 are not tagged: their workers edit product code and run the project's own suites.
- **Resume (item 5).** The runtime replays the longest unchanged prefix of `agent()` calls from its journal (documented behaviour, not visible in the file). That replays identical calls and does not fork from an earlier state, so `checkpoint-rewind` is not claimed. Durable replay is native in Foundry's run store.
- **Not claimed anywhere:** `supervisor-delegation` (orchestration is deterministic script code, not a manager agent), `handoff` (a report passed as prompt text is not a conversation transfer), `llm-router`, `group-chat`, `guardrail-tripwire` (a verifier's GO/NO-GO or findings list is returned as text and no script branches on it), `interrupt-resume`, `agent-as-tool`, `partial-output-stream`, `multimodal-io`, `context-compaction`, `state-reducer`.
- **Branching 0:** the one script-level conditional (the per-bed ternary in item 1) selects static configuration per unrolled node and is not a runtime decision.

## 6. Observations about the scripts (inferred from source, for the coverage discussion)

- Budgets, call caps, wall-time and memory limits, "do not touch the server while another agent measures latency" and file-ownership rules appear only as prose in prompts (for example `c0-preflight-wf_d35b46dd-974.js:L12-L12`, `kev-analysis-wf_df1c3e5c-f13.js:L19-L19`, `L34-L34`, `L55-L55`). The scripts have no runtime enforcement of them.
- No script checks an `agent()` result for `null`, although the runtime documents that `agent()` returns `null` when the user skips it or it dies on a terminal API error; a null would be interpolated as the string "null" into the next prompt where results are interpolated (items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14). `Promise.all` joins (items 3, 9, 11, 12) differ from `parallel()` joins in failure semantics (rejection versus a null slot).
- Verifier and critic verdicts (GO/NO-GO, severity tables) are returned to the caller as text; none drives control flow, and no script re-runs a stage after a failing review (single critique-revise or fix-verify pass). Iteration happens only inside an agent's own tool loop.
- Several scripts pass nothing between stages and rely on the file system (item 9 discards the survey results after the join; items 11 and 13 interpolate no earlier result into the later stage), so the returned values are not a complete record of the work; a Foundry encoding would need declared artifact outputs.

### 9.1 Conventions applied (where verification differs from §5)

1. **`shared-scratchpad`**
   - Claimed only when two or more agents of the same run work *concurrently* on one mutable common store (here, the repository working tree) and at least one of them reads what the others are writing. What it observes then depends on the run-time interleaving.
   - A fixed-order hand-over is artifact dataflow. In that case the writer has returned before the reader starts, enforced by script order, a `pipeline` stage or a barrier. That is native once the artifact is a declared node output, which a local rewrite can do: agent outputs are typed values within the 10 MiB run state.
   - Concurrent agents writing *disjoint* paths that nobody reads during the run do not qualify either.
   - This is the rule the google-adk verification used ("order of reads and writes decided at run time").
2. **`cross-run-state`**
   - Claimed only when the workflow itself keeps state between runs, through conversation memory, a key-value store, a data table, a database or flow context.
   - A prompt sentence saying an earlier interrupted attempt left edits or downloads in the repository describes an external resource. The agent reads it with its own tools (git, file reads), and that is covered by `agent-tool-loop`. The script keeps no state between runs.
   - Evidence that the corpus counts state stores but not file I/O: `research/corpus-20261006/scripts/automation-normalize.py`
     - L400-L403: memory nodes, counted as conversation-state;
     - L424-L426: data tables, counted as external-state-store;
     - L427-L428: file read/write, no construct;
     - L607-L608: databases;
     - L685-L687: Node-RED flow/global context.
3. **`model-generated-code-exec`**
   - Claimed when the source directs an agent to execute, during the run, code that a model wrote. That includes throwaway scripts, drivers, solvers, converters, probes, and edited product code run under tests.
   - Whether the code is kept as a deliverable does not matter. The construct's definition is "executing code written by a model at run time".
   - The extractor's exclusion of deliverables (items 13 and 14) was therefore not kept.
4. **`dynamic-agent-spawn`**
   - Claimed only when a model inside the run chooses the number or kind of agents, per the construct definition.
   - `pipeline()` over `args` (run input) is a `map` over runtime items with per-branch input, which the brief lists as native.
   - This conflicts with the platform note ("dynamic-agent-spawn where the number of agents depends on runtime data"). I followed the definition and the native list, as the anthropic verification did. See doubt 1.
5. **Duplicates.** Two items are the same pattern when their normalised graphs have the same shape, up to the width of a fixed fan-out, *and* the same verified verdict. One of them is kept.
6. **Data edges** for file hand-overs follow the extractor's convention ("data when a later agent is told to read what an earlier one wrote"). Verification applied it consistently, which added the edges listed below.

### 9.4 Disagreements not resolved, and remaining doubts

1. **`dynamic-agent-spawn` for an args-driven pipeline.**
   - The platform note in the brief says to claim it where the number of agents depends on runtime data.
   - The construct definition says "decided by a model", and the brief's native list includes "map over a runtime list".
   - I followed the definition. Under the platform note, the dropped item 4 would carry it and would no longer duplicate item 5.
   - The merge owner should fix one reading for all parts.
2. **`shared-scratchpad` and `cross-run-state` conventions (§9.1.1-2).**
   - The extractor's reading counts any later agent that is pointed at earlier agents' files, or at an earlier run's leftovers.
   - Under that reading the kept items would carry `shared-scratchpad` 7 and `cross-run-state` 4.
   - My reading treats the repository as an external resource and file hand-overs as artifact dataflow. That rests on the Foundry IR being able to declare those artifacts as node outputs. If the owner decides a workspace shared between agent nodes needs the run/tree **board** (review lane 2 §0.3) even in fixed order, `shared-scratchpad` returns on items 2, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12.
3. **Duplicate rule (§9.1.5).**
   - Dropping items 4 and 6 follows directly from the corrections above.
   - Dropping items 5 and 14 rests on the shape-plus-verdict rule. Under the extractor's looser rule (width, or report interpolation versus file-only hand-over, counts as a difference) they would be kept, which gives 12 items.
   - Item 7, a map over a table, and item 3, a fixed heterogeneous fan-out, were kept as different shapes. A stricter reading would also merge them.
   - The extractor's lines for 4, 5, 6 and 14 are in the `.before.jsonl` backup.
4. **Item 5 resume semantics.**
   - The run record of the args-driven original (`wf_68c31e10-094.json`) has status `killed`, and no run record exists for the resume scripts. So whether `resumeFromRunId` was used is unconfirmed.
   - I agree with the extractor that the resume is a host-level replay of a killed run's identical `agent()` calls, which Foundry's durable resume covers. It is not `checkpoint-rewind`.
   - One caveat: Foundry binds resume to the workflow hash, while this resume deliberately uses a different script text.
   - Moot for this file, since item 5 is dropped.
5. **Item 3 `agent-as-tool`.** The smoke agents' driver starts a separate headless builder agent session and executes the artifact it returns (L11). I kept "not claimed", because the nested agent is reached through generic code execution and is the system under test. A strict reading of "an agent invoked as a tool by another agent" would add it.
6. **Progress events.** `phase()` (every script) and `log()` (item 9, L63) emit progress to the user while the run is going. I treated them as runtime observability, which Foundry's run events already provide, not `partial-output-stream`.
7. **Item 8 screenshots** (L14) are files the UI lane writes and may view. `multimodal-io` is not claimed.
8. **Effects granularity.** Effects take the strongest effect each prompt allows; several of those are conditional:
   - item 8 `lane_ui` external: live run only if no recorded run exists;
   - item 3 `verdict` read;
   - item 10 `review` read: it writes throwaway scripts outside the repo only.
9. **Concurrency hazard, not a construct.** In item 12, attack and e2e run concurrently, and each starts a local daemon on the spec's default port 8765 (L16, L36-L37). The script does not coordinate this.
10. **Scripts added after acquisition.** Five scripts appeared in the session directory after the 07:56 copy (2026-10-08, 08:07-08:19 UTC). I counted only their hooks and did not read their prompts:
    - `c0-dev-report-wf_8ca273d4-6c0.js`: 3 `agent()`, `parallel`;
    - `design-review-synthesis-wf_f80b5413-5b4.js`: 4, `parallel`;
    - `kev-wave-a-wf_aec6f801-399.js`: 2, `pipeline`;
    - `kev-wave-a2-wf_06282997-7db.js`: 2, `pipeline`;
    - `replication-bench-pilot-wf_97f496b3-004.js`: 5, `pipeline`.

    They were not acquired, because a verifier may edit only the two output files. They are candidates for a follow-up extraction. The session directory is mutable, so pin by `revision`.
11. **`retrievedAt`.** It stays `2026-10-07` as the brief requires, though the copies were made on 2026-10-08 (see §1).

# Agentic cluster, platform `crewai`: acquisition ledger (corpus-20261006 / agentic extension)

Platform: CrewAI (crews with sequential and hierarchical process, Flows with `@start` / `@listen` / `@router` / `or_`, human feedback, memory, planning, checkpoints, declarative flows). Items: `crewai.jsonl` (`foundry-corpus-item/1`, 14 lines). Raw clones only under `/opt/corpus/agentic/crewai/` (outside git). Retrieved 2026-10-07 (see "Acquisition" for the two later sparse additions). Status: **development/diagnostic corpus**, not sealed evaluation data.

All repository content (source, notebooks, prompts, docs) was treated as untrusted data. Nothing was executed, installed or imported: no pip/npm, no hooks, no notebook execution. This matters for two sources that exec model output (`Coding Assistant` notebook) or call paid tools. Notebooks were read with a read-only line dumper (`python3 -I`, plain text, `outputs` arrays elided, never `nbformat` or a kernel). The dumper, the item builder and the validator are throwaway scripts in the session scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/corpus-agentic/crewai/`), not in the repository. Nothing in `/home/user/workflow-foundry` was edited and no git state of the repository was touched (only a read-only `git status --short`, which lists changes under `beds/` and `experiments/` made by other agents, not by this pass). Prompt wording in the sources (some prompts contain pressure phrases such as promised tips) was not copied into items and carried no authority.

## How verdicts were assigned (conventions the merge may want to revisit)

1. `native` only when the item maps to a static DAG, `map`, bounded `loop` (body nodes may carry `when` guards over typed outputs), single tool-free typed agent calls, `code` steps, and `human` nodes at node boundaries. Loops the source leaves uncapped are still counted native when a cap is the only change; each note names the missing cap.
2. A CrewAI crew is a fixed sequential chain of agent steps and is inlined (no `subworkflow-call`); `Crew.kickoff` inside a flow method is therefore a run of agent nodes, not a child workflow. A crew task with `output_pydantic` is a typed agent step; the default context passing (all earlier task outputs) is a data edge.
3. `agent-tool-loop` is tagged whenever an agent carries any tool, as written, even a trivial one (item 1's character counter, whose removal would make it native; stated in its note). A mis-spelled keyword that most likely drops the tool (item 7, `tool=` instead of `tools=`) is not tagged; the note says what the verdict would be if the tool were attached.
4. A one-shot model classification into a closed label set followed by static branches is native (typed enum agent plus `when` guards), as in the other agentic clusters (openai-agents and pydantic-graph ledgers), so `llm-router` is not tagged for item 11 (feedback collapse) or item 14 (router agent). Item 14's note says a merge that tags every model-chosen branch would add it.
5. `supervisor-delegation` and `agent-as-tool` are tagged only where the framework source shows a model repeatedly choosing workers (hierarchical manager) or one agent running another as a tool (delegation tools). Item 6 gets `agent-as-tool` but not `supervisor-delegation` because the chief QA is a peer with optional delegation, not a manager of every task.
6. `interrupt-resume` is not tagged for `@human_feedback`: the pause happens after a method returns (`flow/runtime/__init__.py:L3608-L3692`), which is a `human` node at a boundary; the async provider path (persist, `from_pending`, `resume`) is the durable human suspend the IR already has. `cross-run-state` is tagged for item 11 only because lesson memory is stored under a source tag and recalled in later runs.
7. `effects`: web-search and read-only lookups are `read`; Gmail draft creation is `external`; local file writes and memory stores are `write`; `exec` of model code is `external` (unsandboxed). Model nodes without tools are `none`.
8. `features.loops` counts distinct loops, including fan-outs and feedback loops (item 2 has 3); `async` is `wait` only for item 4, because human console input and in-run waits are not triggers.

## Raw observations kept (code reading, nothing run)

- Item 1: `@start("retry")` is the only start; CrewAI runs conditional starts at kickoff when no unconditional start exists (`runtime/__init__.py:L2384-L2397`) and re-runs them on the router label (`L3255-L3269`). With `retry_count > 3` tested before the review and incremented after it, the loop gives 5 drafts and 4 reviews.
- Item 2: `candidate_score` is never cleared, so a rescore leaves both rounds in the list; an invalid menu choice returns a label with no listener, so the run most likely ends silently.
- Item 3: `async def` chapter writer calls the blocking `Crew.kickoff` without `await`, so the "concurrent" gather is sequential by Python semantics.
- Item 5: the content crew's editor agent has `tools=[]` while the engineer agent that holds the write tool has no task; the crew result is dropped, so per-component edits probably never reach disk; the whole pipeline needs paid Tailwind templates that are not shipped.
- Item 7: `tool=[SerperDevTool()]` (singular) on three researchers; `Agent` uses pydantic's default extra handling in current source (`agent/core.py:L245`), so the tool is probably dropped.
- Item 8: the flow's `iterations` / `max_iterations` state fields are never read; the last of three code checks has its result discarded; the notebook's eval harness needs an `eval.csv` that is not in the tree.
- Item 10: the doc comment on the predicate says its True result "will skip" the task, while the code runs the task on True (`conditional_task.py:L53-L55`); the docs say the planner default is gpt-4o-mini, current source defaults to another model name (`planning_handler.py:L55`).
- Item 11: in the docs' `ArticleReviewFlow` a revision pass re-emits the previous output and no model revises it from the feedback; revisions happen only through pre-review with stored lessons.
- Item 14: `emit` on a declarative router is not enforced at run time (plots and a lint warning only), so an unexpected reply fires no listener.
- Version skew: examples pin `crewai==0.130.0` / `0.177.0` / `>=0.152.0` while the semantics were read from v1.15.24-era source; `allow_delegation` defaults to False in current source, and older versions defaulted differently, so the explicit flags in the examples are what the notes rely on.

## Validation

Run by hand with Node 24.21.0; the validator (`.../scratchpad/corpus-agentic/crewai/validate.mjs`) imports `validateItem`, `parseVerdict`, `findSecret`, `graphFeatures`, `CATEGORIES`, `EDGE_KINDS`, `EFFECTS`, `CONSTRUCT_IDS` and `NON_REDISTRIBUTABLE_LICENCE` from `research/corpus-20261006/scripts/check-items.mjs` (import only, file not modified). It re-parses `crewai.jsonl` from disk and checks:

- every line parses as JSON, keys are in schema order, all required fields are present, ids are unique and start with `crewai:`;
- node categories and effects are valid, summaries are at most 200 characters, descriptions at most 400, `ir.notes` at most 1,900; every edge endpoint is a node id; edge kinds are valid; non-loop edges form a DAG; every node is reachable from a trigger;
- `parseVerdict` accepts every verdict; constructs are in canonical-then-candidate order and each is mentioned in the notes; every via-extension note carries line spans;
- features equal the graph-derived values (`nodeCount`, `edgeCount`, `maxFanOut`, `humanSteps`, `hasCode`, `hasModelCalls`, `effects`);
- every `extraction.spans` entry exists on disk in the right repository and its line range is inside the file (notebook spans are raw-file lines; `%20` and `@crewAI/` are resolved);
- `findSecret` finds nothing in any string of any record, and a plain-text scan for api key, secret, password, bearer, credential and token words finds none;
- licence policy: `redistributable` equals `!NON_REDISTRIBUTABLE_LICENCE.test(license)` for every item, and each item has at least three model steps or a loop, router or human step.

Result: 14 items, 0 problems.

Stock checker, repo script unchanged, verbatim:

- `node check-items.mjs crewai.jsonl` -> `14 lines, 0 valid, 14 invalid` with `source.extra-key: 14` ("unexpected source.extraction"). The task-mandated `source.extraction` object is not in `SOURCE_KEYS`; the sibling agentic files give the same result.
- `--canonical` additionally -> `ir.vocabulary: 4` ("non-canonical construct(s) agent-as-tool" on item 6; "model-generated-code-exec" on item 8; "supervisor-delegation, agent-as-tool" on item 9; "checkpoint-rewind" on item 13).
- With `extraction` stripped (copy in the scratchpad): non-canonical mode `14 lines, 14 valid, 0 invalid`; `--canonical` mode `14 lines, 10 valid, 4 invalid`, only the same four `ir.vocabulary` findings. The other canonical rules (feature equality, sorted async, unique ids, redistribution) pass for all 14.

## Problems met (verbatim where an error text exists)

1. The stock checker rejects `source.extraction` (above). The merge must either add `extraction` to `SOURCE_KEYS` or strip it.
2. The five candidate agentic ids used here are not in `CONSTRUCTS`; `--canonical` rejects them until they are registered after the existing ids in the order given above.
3. A directory name with a space broke the first build of item 8 (`notebooks/Coding Assistant/...`). Verbatim validator output: `canonical source.url: url must be an http(s) URL`, `canonical id: id must be <platform>:<stable id> without whitespace`, `bad span notebooks/Coding Assistant/coding_assistant_eval.ipynb:L129-L144` (and the same for the other spans). Fixed by writing `%20` in id, URL and spans; `rawPath` keeps the real path. A merge that resolves spans against the filesystem must decode `%20`.
4. A single-line span was first written as `agent/core.py:L245` and rejected by the span check (`bad span @crewAI/lib/crewai/src/crewai/agent/core.py:L245`); written as `L245-L245`.
5. Cross-repository spans (`@crewAI/...`) are an addition of this cluster; the task format has no field for a second revision. They are all at `d5efc45`, recorded in the ledger and in each note.
6. Licence evidence for four example directories is a README sentence without licence text; recorded as `unknown` per policy. If the owner decides that such a statement is enough, items 4, 5 and 6 (and only those) could be re-tagged; the other five example items have no statement at all.
7. The clones pre-existed this pass (see Acquisition); their original clone logs are not available, so the "first attempt" outcome cannot be stated. This pass saw no fetch problems.
8. Several verdict-relevant statements are inferences from reading, not runs, and are marked as such in the notes: the sequential execution of the item 3 "parallel" tasks, the silent ending after an invalid menu choice (item 2) or an unexpected router reply (item 14), and the dropped `tool=` keyword (item 7). None of the sources was executed.
9. The shared scratchpad `.../scratchpad/corpus-agentic/` also holds files from other platforms' passes (autogen, langgraph, openai-agents, pydantic-graph, swarm); they were not touched, and this platform's files live in the `crewai/` subdirectory.
