- **Observed code.** Every node, edge, loop and effect comes from the pinned files; spans are in `source.extraction.spans` and in each `ir.notes` (paths relative to the repo root; where a note gives a bare file name after a full path in the same note, the bare name is that file, e.g. `run.py` is the item's own file and `agents.py` is `src/smolagents/agents.py`). All spans were machine-checked against the line counts of the checkout.
- **Documentation claims.** The Open Deep Research README states 55% pass@1 on GAIA validation against 67% for the original (`README.md:L8`); the RAG page lists the advantages of agentic retrieval (`rag.md:L36-L37`); the guided tour says a failing check "will log the error message and continue the run" (`guided_tour.md:L398`); the memory tutorial says screenshots are pruned "to save on token costs" (`memory.md:L59`). None was re-run.
- **Inference.** (a) All IR verdicts are static judgments against the Phase 1 IR (`schemas/workflow.schema.json`, `research/core-20261006/DESIGN.md`), not compile or run results. (b) The defects in section 8 are static readings. (c) Item 6's graph is drawn from `agents.py` and `memory.py`; the tour's snippet only supplies the validator and the task. (d) Effects were assigned from tool code, not declared by the framework.
- **Unavailable.** A live model or search key, the gated GAIA and benchmark datasets (`smolagents/GAIA-annotated`, `smolagents/benchmark-v1`), a Chrome or Helium install, repository history before the pinned commit (depth 1), any execution of the tests.

## 7. IR notes worth carrying forward

- The managed-agent mechanism needs the executor to know the callee by name (`agents.py:L490-L492`), which is why remote executors refuse it (`agents.py:L1609`). A Foundry executor for `agent-as-tool` should state whether the callee runs in the same sandbox.
- `final_answer` leaves the executor through a `BaseException` so model code cannot catch it (`local_python_executor.py:L1572-L1581`). Any Foundry equivalent of code-as-action needs the same non-catchable terminal call.
- Cancellation (`agent.interrupt()`) is cooperative and checked only at the start of an iteration (`agents.py:L545-L547`): one more action runs after a cancel. A Foundry cancel should state at which boundary side effects stop.

## 8. Observed defects and negative results (static reading, nothing executed)

Kept so that later runs do not mistake source defects for Foundry defects.

Item 6 / guided tour
- The documented check `is_integer(final_answer, agent_memory=None)` (`docs/source/en/guided_tour.md:L376`) has no parameter named `agent`, but every check is called as `check(final_answer, memory, agent=self)` (`agents.py:L616`). The call raises `TypeError`, which `_validate_final_answer` turns into an `AgentError` (`agents.py:L617-L618`), so the documented example can never be accepted and would run to the step cap (20) and return the fallback answer. The library's own tests use three parameters (`tests/test_agents.py:L667-L668`, `L678`). The page also says checks take "the agent itself as parameters" (`guided_tour.md:L395`).

Item 2 / `run_gaia.py`
- `get_total_token_counts()` returns a `TokenUsage` dataclass without `__getitem__` (`monitoring.py:L37-L45`, `L89-L93`), but `run_gaia.py:L100-L102` and `L254-L255` index it with `["input"]`; `L197-L200` builds a plain dict that is later used with attribute access. By static reading the search agent's `final_answer_checks` hook raises on every final answer (the answer is rejected and the agent runs to its 20-step cap) and the run raises outside its `try` after the first worker finishes.
- `L238` tests `"AgentParsingError" in step` for `ChatMessage` objects, a dataclass with no `__contains__` or `__iter__` (`models.py:L124-L158`); the `TypeError` would fall into the `except` at `L244` and store a null prediction.
- `get_examples_to_answer` keeps only rows with a non-empty `file_name` (`L284`), so questions without attachments are never run. The example command in the header uses `--concurrency 32` (`L1`), above the IR's `map` cap of 16.

Item 3 / `plan_customization.py`
- "Cancel" calls `agent.interrupt()` from the planning callback; the flag is read at the top of the next iteration (`agents.py:L545-L547`), so action step 1 (model call, code, search) still runs. The library test calls `interrupt()` from an action-step callback (`tests/test_agents.py:L1429-L1450`).
- The `else:` at `plan_customization.py:L161-L162` belongs to the inner `try`, so a successful resume prints "An error occurred" with the earlier exception and the resumed result is never printed.

Item 4 / `web_browser.md`
- The doc version of `search_item_ctrl_f` splices the model-supplied text into an XPath expression (`web_browser.md:L54`); the library module of the same example escapes it (`vision_web_browser.py:L87-L121`) and has tests for injection strings (`tests/test_vision_web_browser.py:L56-L77`, `L78-L130`). The doc has no call that closes the browser.
- Executor state: `LocalPythonExecutor.state` is created once (`local_python_executor.py:L1716`) and nothing in it is reset by `agent.run` (`agents.py:L478-L480` resets memory and monitor only). The doc's second request runs on the same agent, so variables from the first request stay visible to the model's code. Not a documented feature.

Item 7 / `smolagents_benchmark/run.py`
- `L99` prints `eval_ds["simpleqa"]` by name and raises if that configuration is absent. In `vanilla` mode `L157` asks the `Model` object for `.monitor`, which `models.py` does not define, so the exception path would store the error text as the answer. `start_time` is a float and `end_time` is later overwritten by a string (`L152`, `L165`, `L171`). The function default for workers is 32 (`L196`) against the CLI default of 8 (`L72-L77`).

Item 1 / `run.py`
- `GoogleSearchTool(provider="serper")` raises at construction if the key variable is unset (`default_tools.py:L175-L188`), and `login(os.getenv("HF_TOKEN"))` runs at import (`run.py:L29`), so the script cannot start without both secrets. No credential value was read.

2. *Item 5 `partial-output-stream` is borderline.* `stream_outputs=True` makes the library render tokens to the console while `run()` returns only the final answer (rag.py:L64, L67). I kept it on observable behaviour, consistent with the openai-agents routing item, where the script prints deltas itself. If the construct requires a stream delivered to the calling code, this is an FP and the verdict becomes `via-extension:agent-tool-loop+model-generated-code-exec`. Item 5 is also a single agent with one tool and 4 steps. It meets the loop rule and is the cluster's only index-then-retrieve shape, so it is kept and flagged.
3. *`error-branch` is not claimed for items 2 and 7.* Both catch any exception around the agent run and record it (run_gaia.py:L224-L251; run.py:L154-L170). I kept the extractor's reading: `onError: continue` plus a `when` guard, the "partial" emulation the CONSTRUCTS registry names. That holds only if the extended agent node keeps `onError`; today `onError` exists on `task` and `agent` only. If the lead rules otherwise, add `error-branch` to both.
4. *`supervisor-delegation` in items 1 and 2 has a single worker.* The manager decides at every step whether to call `search_agent` again (run.py:L101-L109). I kept the construct by its definition. The openai-agents verification flagged the same borderline case (its doubt 3).
5. *Item 3 `interrupt-resume` rests on the agent loop being one node.* The pause is a blocking `input()` inside a step callback, not a durable suspension. If the loop were unrolled into plan, act and human nodes, today's `human` node would cover the approval and edit paths. The cooperative cancel and the `reset=False` resume would still need the construct.
6. *Item 4.* `context-compaction` trims only images; it does not summarise text (web_browser.md:L96-L98). `new-live-session-handle` depends on the cluster keeping one shared definition.

They differ structurally: item 2 has a team, model pre-captioning and post-reformulation, while item 7 has a sequential outer loop, a three-way agent switch and a Hub push. Both are kept. A stricter "no benchmark harnesses" bar would drop item 7 first.

## 1. Acquisition

Three repos, shallow and sparse. The brief named `sdk-python` and `samples`; `tools` was added because the Workflow tool the brief lists (and the swarm and A2A client tools the samples call) lives there, not in the other two (`git ls-tree` of sdk-python and samples has no workflow tool; `site/.../workflow.mdx:L93-L95` only points to it).

```sh
mkdir -p /opt/corpus/agentic/strands && cd /opt/corpus/agentic/strands
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/strands-agents/sdk-python.git sdk-python
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/strands-agents/samples.git samples
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/strands-agents/tools.git tools
# then, per clone, git sparse-checkout set --no-cone <paths>  (sets below)
```

All three succeeded on the first attempt through the agent proxy: no 403/407, no TLS error, no reset. Verified in each clone: `rev-list --count HEAD` is 1, `remote.origin.partialclonefilter = blob:none`, `core.sparseCheckout = true`, no `.gitmodules` in the tree, and the only `.gitattributes` (sdk-python root) is `* text=auto eol=lf`, so no LFS and no submodules.

## 4. Modelling conventions used in this file

- Node ids are short snake_case names of the source concept; `type` names the Strands concept (`agent+tools`, `agent-as-tool`, `custom-node`, `interrupt`, `steering-handler`, `a2a-remote-agent`, ...). Categories follow `CATEGORIES`: model calls are `model`; an LLM judge is `model`; deterministic hooks, edge predicates and routers are `condition`; a remote A2A agent is `subworkflow`; the model-written tool files in item 10 and the checker in item 1 are `code`; an interrupt is `human`.
- Tools stay inside their agent node when they are plain tools (as in the sibling clusters) except where they carry the semantics of the item (items 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11), where they are separate nodes. A tool returning to its agent is a `loop` edge, so `features.loops` is the number of `loop`-kind edges in the graph. `features.branching` counts decision points (condition nodes plus model-chosen branches); it is never below the number of condition nodes (the merge floors it).
- Edge conditions in Strands are attached to edges, not nodes; a `condition` node stands for them (`decision`, `can_renew`, `decision_router`). Framework steps that exist only in the library (the swarm handoff step, the steering ledger, the stop-reason router) are modelled as nodes because the verdict depends on them.
- `async`: `wait` where a run suspends for a human (items 4, 5), `webhook` where the runtime is an HTTP endpoint (items 5, 6), `poll` and `schedule` for item 10. `effects` follow what the tool does as written; where a tool list was not read (the DynamoDB MCP server in item 6, the SQL tool in item 7) the effect is the one the code comment or prompt states and the note says so.
- Where the IR could express the intended workflow but not the library's literal semantics (item 7's any-edge join), the graph records the intended reading and the note records the divergence; no construct was invented for it.

## 6. Facts about the sources worth carrying into any later analysis

Each is also in the relevant item's `ir.notes`; labels say whether it was read (observed) or reasoned (inferred, not run).

- Graph join (inferred): `Graph` fires a node as soon as any incoming edge from the batch that just finished is satisfied (`strands-py/src/strands/multiagent/graph.py:L946-L978`; documented as OR semantics at `site/.../multi-agent/graph.mdx:L192-L215`), so an asymmetric fan-in such as item 7's synthesizer would run early and again; the resume path uses AND semantics (`graph.py:L1429-L1430`). The sample locks an older SDK (1.13.0), so the trace is unverified for it.
- Graph data flow (inferred): a node sees the original task plus only direct predecessors' outputs (`graph.py:L1158-L1242`), so item 1's writer does not receive its own earlier draft on revisit and its finalizer does not receive the draft.
- `invocation_state` persistence (observed doc/code mismatch): `graph.mdx:L184-L188` says it is serialised with the checkpoint; `serialize_state` (`graph.py:L1270-L1293`) lists no such field and a comment at `graph.py:L1422-L1427` says the caller passes it on resume. Item 5 works anyway because a missing risk score fails to human.
- Swarm (observed): `max_handoffs` and `max_iterations` compare the same counter (`swarm.py:L210-L215`); hitting any limit yields FAILED (`swarm.py:L799-L802`); the notebook's `complete_swarm_task` tool does not exist in sdk-python (only in the notebook text and in `strands_tools/swarm.py` docstrings).
- Steering (observed): handler exceptions are swallowed, so a failing steering check lets the call through (`steering/core/handler.py:L97-L101`, `L142-L148`).
- Workflow tool (inferred from reading, not run): a failed task with dependents makes `start_workflow` loop forever; a restarted workflow never counts already-completed tasks; per-task `timeout` is stored but never enforced; `pause` and `resume` are stubs; `WorkflowManager` is a singleton that keeps the first parent agent. No test covers any of these.
- Self-improving agent (inferred): the interactive agent and the ambient thread share one `Agent`, whose SDK default rejects overlapping calls (`agent.py:L325-L327`); shell and file_write prompt the console unless `BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT=true`, which the notebooks set and the code files do not.

### Conventions applied (so the merge can reconcile)

1. **`llm-router`** is claimed when a model's tool call or free output passes control to one of two or more declared agents or nodes and the chooser does not get the answer back (multi-target handoff, as in item 3). It is not claimed in two cases:
   - when a manager picks among agent-tools inside its own tool loop, which `agent-tool-loop+supervisor-delegation+agent-as-tool` covers (openai-agents, pydantic-graph, smolagents, llamaindex, crewai, anthropic, mastra);
   - for a one-shot typed or closed-label classifier with code branching, which is native as `agent` role `route` plus `when`.

   google-adk tags every supervisor choice as `llm-router`; under that rule items 2, 6 and 7 would keep it.
2. **`handoff`** is kept for the Strands Swarm although the transfer is a message plus a shared board, not the transcript (item 3 note). The agent transfers control itself mid-turn with a tool, which is the platform's handoff mechanism; the openai-agents and ag2 swarm items are tagged the same way.
3. **Edge kinds:** a tool's return to its agent, and any edge that carries state into a later iteration, turn or run, is a `loop` edge. After these fixes every graph is a DAG once `loop` edges are removed, and every `loop` edge closes a cycle; the extractor's file had cycles over non-loop edges in items 4, 6, 9, 10 and 11.

### Disagreements and doubts not resolved

1. **`llm-router` boundary** (items 2, 6, 7). This is convention 1. Under the google-adk rule all three regain it. A merge should fix one rule for all clusters.
2. **Item 10 `poll-trigger`.** The ambient thread polls in-process idle state, not an external source (`ambient.py:L43-L69`). If the interactive session counts as one run, the idle trigger is a wait for the next user message with a 20 s timeout. That is `signal-wait`, and `async` would be `wait` rather than `poll`. Kept as the extractor had it and noted in the item.
3. **Item 3 `handoff`.** Conversation transfer is partial (convention 2). A strict reading of "control AND conversation transfer" would leave only `llm-router+shared-scratchpad` plus a native loop of typed agent steps.
4. **`webhook-trigger` for AgentCore-hosted entrypoints** (items 5, 6). An AgentCore invocation is an authenticated API call carrying an input payload, close to an explicit run start. The tag is kept to match the autogen (FastAPI) and semantic-kernel (gRPC) items.
5. **Item 6 hidden session state.** The module-level orchestrator accumulates conversation across requests in one container. If AgentCore maps one runtime session to one container, this is a de facto `chat-session`. Not claimed.
6. **Item 4 `chat-session`.** The two scripted requests share conversation history through the session manager. Only `cross-run-state` is claimed, because the behaviour under test depends on the trust key.
7. **Library-level oracles.** Items 1, 3 and 5 label the SDK's own mocked unit tests of the same mechanism as `mocked-execution`, as the dspy and langgraph clusters do. A stricter rule (an oracle must run the item's own workflow) would make them `none`.
8. **Item 7 join semantics.** The graph records the intended join-all. Python Graph at HEAD uses documented OR semantics (`graph.mdx:L192-L196`), so the synthesizer and the report writer would run twice. The sample locks strands-agents 1.13.0, which is not in the clones. Either reading is native (an unrolled DAG), so the verdict does not depend on it.
9. **Item 8 retry.** The "no retry on structured-output failure" split is an error-class condition, so `adaptive-retry` could be argued. Kept native through `loop` plus `onError: continue` plus `until` on the error code. This assumes the IR's handled-error output exposes the error class; that was not verified in `src/runtime.mjs`.
10. **Item 11 scope.** The item is the Workflow tool (an engine whose task graph the parent model writes), not one concrete workflow. It is kept because the brief names it. Create-then-start-by-id could also be read as `subworkflow-call`; it is not claimed, because `dynamic-dag` (plan/expand) covers the authored plan.
11. **Item 9 oracle kind** stays `test-profile` although model-free unit tests exist for the guardrail predicates; `mocked-execution` is defensible.
12. **Versions.** The semantics are read at sdk-python HEAD, while the samples lock 1.13.0, 1.30.0 and 1.35.0 (section 8, problem 5). Still unresolved.
13. **Stub effects.** `delete_files`, `send_confirmation` and the order catalogue are stubs or in-memory dicts, classified by what they stand for (write/external), as the extractor did.
